title: Product PRD: Redwood Optimize v3 - Launch Plan and Specs
author: Priya Patel
body:
Overview:

This document describes the product requirements, design specifications, roadmap, pricing/packaging strategy, and release notes for Redwood Optimize v3 (RWO v3). RWO v3 is the next major iteration of Redwood's cost/performance toolkit focused on automated quantization recommendations, dynamic batching policies, and quality-aware caching for hosted and dedicated deployments. The primary goal for v3 is to reduce per-token inference cost by 20-35% for representative customers while maintaining model-quality regression < 0.5% as measured on guardrail evals.

Goals and success metrics:

- Primary goals:
  - Reduce average per-token cost by 25% for English text-generation workloads across the Redwood model catalog.
  - Improve median 95th-percentile tail latency by 10% under typical production load.
  - Provide transparent, actionable recommendations customers can apply in 3 clicks from Console.
- Key success metrics (measured at 30/60/90 days post-launch):
  - Cost reduction: median -25% across pilot customers (target: >= 20%).
  - Quality regressions: < 0.5% measured by Redwood eval harness on canonical prompt sets.
  - Adoption: 30% of customers with >100K monthly tokens adopting at least one Optimize suggestion within 60 days.
  - Console conversion: 10% uplift in self-serve Dedicated trials that enable Optimize.

Scope and out-of-scope:

- In-scope for v3:
  - Automatic quantization profile suggestions (FP16 -> int8/awq) with safety checks and rollback.
  - Dynamic batching policy engine with per-route suggestions and simulated cost/latency previews.
  - Quality-aware KV/prefix caching: detect stable prefixes and offer cache policies.
  - Console UI: recommendation center with 1-click apply, preview, and rollback.
  - API: new /optimize/suggestions endpoint, dry-run mode, and apply endpoint for programmatic workflows.
- Out-of-scope for v3:
  - Model-training or finetuning recommendations.
  - Private (air-gapped) on-prem installer for v3; included observability exports only.

Requirements (high-level and detailed):

- Functional requirements:
  1. SuggestQuantizationProfiles: For a given model and workload profile, return N ranked quantization profiles with estimated cost, latency, and quality delta.
  2. SimulateBatchingPolicy: Accept route configuration and simulated traffic distribution to estimate throughput and 95th latency.
  3. RecommendCachePolicies: Identify prefixes with high hit-rate potential and recommend TTL, shard, and key strategies.
  4. OneClickApply: Console action that applies a recommended profile to a selected route with canary rollout options.
  5. DryRun mode: All apply actions must support dry-run to produce expected cost/latency impact without changing serving configuration.

- Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
  - Security: All recommendation payloads must respect RBAC; apply endpoints require 'optimize.apply' permission.
  - Reliability: Suggestion engine SLA 99.5 availability; suggestions should be returned within 2s for cached profiles and within 10s for full simulation jobs.
  - Scale: Support concurrent recommendations for 5k routes across Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
  - Observability: Emit metrics for suggestion count, acceptance rate, simulated cost delta, and quality delta.
  - Auditability: Every apply/rollback event must write an immutable audit log with actor, timestamp, and pre/post config.

Design Spec (technical):

1) Architecture overview:

- Components:
  - Optimize Engine (service): hosts quantization simulator, batching simulator, and caching analyzer.
  - Data Ingest Pipeline: collects per-route token distribution, sequence length histogram, KV-hit traces, and past latency traces (30 days window).
  - Recommendation Store: stores candidate profiles, simulation outputs, and acceptance metadata.
  - Console Integration: Recommendation Center UI + apply workflows + canary rollout orchestrator.
  - API Gateway: /optimize endpoints secured by RBAC and rate limits.

- Interaction flow (high-level):
  1. Data pipeline aggregates workload telemetry into Optimize Engine (batch window 1h, realtime sampling at 1%).
  2. Optimize Engine runs fast-path heuristics for common models and cached suggestions (<2s).
  3. For detailed simulation, engine spins a sandbox job (10s-120s depending on route complexity) to produce estimated delta.
  4. Results are surfaced in Console and Recommendation Store; customers can preview and apply.

2) Quantization simulator details:

- Inputs: model meta (architecture, layer shapes), representative corpus (sampled requests), baseline FP16 trace.
- Outputs: estimated throughput, memory footprint, quality delta (scored using Redwood eval harness), compatibility notes (e.g., kernels incompatible on older GPUs).
- Safety checks: if estimated quality delta > 0.5% drop, mark 'requires human review'.

3) Batching policy engine:

- Decision variables: target latency SLO, max batch size, batch timeout, per-route priority.
- Simulator produces curve: throughput vs p50/p95 latency.
- Recommended policy includes suggested batch_timeout_ms and max_batch_size plus expected improvement.

4) Caching analyzer:

- Detects stable prefixes (using 30d sliding window) and computes hit-rate, cost-savings estimate, and eviction TTL suggestions.

Design constraints and tradeoffs:

- Simulations are estimates; we provide clear confidence bands (low/medium/high) based on input sample size.
- Some quantization profiles may require specialized kernel support; recommendations will include downgrade paths.

Roadmap and themes (quarterly):

- Q1 (pilot & internal trials):
  - Launch internal pilot with 3 enterprise customers (finance, ecomm, search) and Redwood's own platform routes.
  - Implement Console Recommendation Center v1 and /optimize/suggestions API.
- Q2 (public beta):
  - Open beta to Hosted customers; add canary orchestration and dry-run APIs.
  - Add multi-model support and cross-route batching suggestions.
- Q3 (general availability):
  - GA for Hosted and Dedicated tiers; add billing-linked cost-credits for accepted suggestions.
  - Start packaging Limited Private deployment connectors for on-prem telemetry.
- Q4 (optimization and adoption):
  - Improve simulator accuracy, add support for custom quantization plugins, and increased automation for trusted customers.

Pricing and packaging notes:

- Pricing goals: align incentives so customers see direct cost savings while Redwood captures a fraction of realized savings for managed services.
- Proposed packaging:
  - Free tier: basic recommendations and dry-run reports for all Hosted customers.
  - Optimize Pro (paid add-on): automatic apply, canary orchestration, and advanced simulations.
  - Enterprise package: dedicated Optimize Engine SLA, on-prem telemetry connectors, and premium support.
- Billing model options considered:
  1. Percent-of-savings (15% of realized monthly cost reduction) - aligns incentives but increases billing complexity.
  2. Fixed subscription tiers (starter/pro/enterprise) - simpler for sales; target uplift: Pro for customers with >$10K/mo spend.
  3. Credits: one-time credit for first-time accepted apply suggestions for self-serve signups.
- Recommendation: launch with Fixed subscription tiers and pilot percent-of-savings for a small set of enterprise customers to validate economics.

Launch plan and rollout steps:

1. Pre-launch (2-4 weeks):
  - Complete security review and privacy impact assessment.
  - Finalize UI copy, telemetry consent, and RBAC rules.
  - Seed Recommendation Store with internal baselines and pilot customer data.
2. Pilot (4-6 weeks):
  - Run pilot with 3 customers; collect acceptance metrics, quality deltas, and performance data.
  - Iterate on simulator thresholds and canary procedures.
3. Beta (6-8 weeks):
  - Open beta to Hosted customers; increase observability retention to 90 days for Optimize-related telemetry.
  - Validate billing path for Pro subscriptions.
4. GA (target date dependent on pilot results):
  - Ramp to general availability for Hosted and Dedicated customers.
  - Publish release notes, migration guide, and playbook for support.

Release notes (initial beta release - v3.0.0-beta):

- Highlights:
  - Introduced Optimize v3 Recommendation Center in Console.
  - Added API endpoints: POST /optimize/suggestions (dry-run), POST /optimize/apply (requires optimize.apply).
  - Initial quantization simulator with AWQ/int8 profile suggestions for curated models.
  - Dynamic batching simulator and cache-policy analyzer.
- Known limitations and caveats:
  - Quantization recommendations not supported on all GPU types; kernel compatibility note included in UI.
  - Private on-prem installer support is limited in beta; telemetry connectors are experimental.
  - Percent-of-savings billing not enabled for beta customers.
- Rollback and mitigation plan:
  1. Any applied change triggers a canary: 1% of traffic for 30 minutes monitored for latency and quality regressions.
  2. Automated rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% or quality delta exceeds 0.5% on guardrail evals.
  3. Manual rollback instructions for support engineers included in eng-runbooks.

Ownership and stakeholders:

- Product: Priya Patel (PM owner)
- Eng: Ethan Moore (backend), Sofia Alvarez (Console/UX), Miguel Rivera (simulator)
- Applied ML & Evals: Dr. Chen Li (quality metrics)
- Security & Compliance: Anika Shah (review and audit)
- Sales & GTM: Nora King (packaging and pilot coordination)

Open questions and decisions to make before GA:

- Billing model: percent-of-savings pilot approval and legal review timeline.
- Default safety thresholds: should the quality delta threshold be 0.5% or 0.2% for high-risk verticals?
- Private deployer support: timeline for on-prem connector beyond telemetry exports.

Appendices:

A) Example API snippets:

- Obtain suggestions (dry-run):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/optimize/suggestions" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"route_id":"route-123","sample_window_minutes":60,"modes":["quantize","batching","cache"]}'

- Apply suggestion (canary):
  curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/optimize/apply" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"suggestion_id":"sugg-456","canary_fraction":0.01,"max_canary_minutes":30}'

B) Example recommendation table (sample):

| suggestion_id | type | estimated_cost_delta | est_p95_delta | confidence | actionable |
| sugg-456 | quantize-awq | -28% | +2% | high | 1-click apply |
| sugg-789 | batching | -12% | -5% | medium | requires canary |

C) Support playbook (summary):

1. Detect: Alert when apply fails or canary monitors exceed thresholds.
2. Triage: Run simulator in dry-run against recent telemetry, verify input sample size, and escalate to simulator owner.
3. Mitigate: Trigger automated rollback and notify customer with root-cause and next steps.
